description: DEF CON 32 War Stories features first-hand accounts from seasoned security researchers, investigators, and defenders detailing high-profile investigations and complex vulnerability discoveries. Presentations explore real-world digital forensics, reverse engineering operations, supply chain compromises, and federal law enforcement operations.

talks.title: Why Are You Still Using My Server for Your Internet Access?
talks.teaser: Details a year-long investigation running eight wpad.tld domains that received over one billion DNS requests and enabled unauthenticated traffic interception.
talks.summary:
The 25-Year-Old WPAD Design Flaw

Web Proxy Auto-Discovery (WPAD) allows client operating systems to automatically discover and configure proxy servers. However, legacy queries falling back to top-level domains create severe interception vulnerabilities.

Registering Top Level WPAD Domains

Researchers registered eight distinct wpad.tld domains and monitored incoming DNS queries over a twelve-month observation period.

Harvesting One Billion DNS Requests

The infrastructure captured over one billion DNS lookups and six hundred gigabytes of Apache web server logs containing sensitive client credentials and internal network metadata.

Executing Man-in-the-Middle Traps

Because clients automatically accept downloaded proxy configuration scripts, attackers controlling these domains can establish man-in-the-middle proxies, decrypt traffic, and serve arbitrary malicious payloads.

talks.title: Xiaomi the Money: Our Toronto Pwn2Own Exploit & BTS Story
talks.teaser: Recounts NCC Group's Pwn2Own Toronto exploit chain compromising the Xiaomi 13 Pro via malicious hyperlinks and app store vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
Pwn2Own Toronto Mobile Target

At the Pwn2Own Toronto competition, security researchers from NCC Group targeted the Xiaomi 13 Pro flagship smartphone to demonstrate full remote device compromise.

Chaining Web Hyperlinks and App Store Flaws

The successful exploit chain leveraged a malicious HTML hyperlink to trigger internal browser handlers and interact with the pre-installed Xiaomi app store to stage unauthorized application installation.

Regional Execution Variations and Field Testing

Vulnerability research revealed that specific app store logic only executed within certain geographic regions, requiring researchers to travel internationally to validate exploit reliability before competition day.

Defensive Hardening by Manufacturers

Evaluating vendor-specific mitigation barriers highlights the extensive engineering efforts modern device manufacturers deploy to prevent remote exploitation in competitive environments.

talks.title: Solving the Lover, Stalker, Killer Murder with Strings, Grep, and Perl
talks.teaser: Goes behind the scenes of a high-profile homicide investigation to show how command-line utilities and digital evidence unmasked an online stalker.
talks.summary:
A Digital Homicide Investigation

Following the disappearance of Cari Farver, an online impostor maintained deceptive digital communications for over three years, using proxies and VPNs to impersonate the victim.

Unmasking Anonymized Digital Traces

Digital forensics investigators untangled extensive layers of anonymizing applications, spoofed email headers, and IP proxy logs to locate the true origin of the communications.

Command Line Forensics with Grep and Perl

Utilizing standard open-source Linux utilities including strings, grep, and bespoke Perl parsing scripts enabled investigators to process vast datasets of raw phone dumps and server logs.

Proving a No-Body Homicide Case

Correlating digital timestamps and forensic artifacts provided the definitive evidentiary trail that proved the homicide in court and secured a criminal conviction.

talks.title: Social Engineering Like You’re Picard
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how generative AI tools enhance phishing and vishing operations and outlines strategies to build organizational situational awareness.
talks.summary:
The AI Revolution in Social Engineering

Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot enable attackers to rapidly generate highly authentic pretexting materials, personalized phishing lures, and believable synthetic vishing dialog.

Simulating Next Generation Attack Campaigns

Red team practitioners leverage AI assistants to craft sophisticated phishing infrastructure, automate reconnaissance on targets, and adapt communication styles dynamically.

Transitioning from Security to Situational Awareness

Traditional compliance-focused security awareness training fails to prepare employees for adaptive AI threats. Organizations must cultivate an active situational awareness mindset.

Turning Threats into Teachable Moments

Adversarial simulations should be used constructively to empower staff, identify organizational blind spots, and foster a supportive security culture.

talks.title: Breaking Network Crypto in Popular Chinese Keyboard Apps
talks.teaser: Exposes flawed custom network encryption in popular Chinese IME keyboard apps that allow network eavesdroppers to intercept keystrokes from 800 million users.
talks.summary:
Cloud Predictive Chinese IME Architecture

Popular Chinese Input Method Editor (IME) keyboards transmit keystroke telemetry to cloud servers to provide character prediction and candidate suggestions for complex scripts.

Flaws in Proprietary Network Encryption

Security analysis of leading Chinese keyboard applications revealed that vendors routinely roll their own custom cryptographic protocols rather than standard TLS implementations.

Systematic Keylogging Exploitation

Cryptanalytic attacks against Sogou IME, Baidu IME, and iFlytek IME demonstrated that passive network eavesdroppers can completely decrypt live keystroke streams from over 800 million active users.

Advocating for HTTPS Everywhere

Remediating systemic keyboard vulnerabilities requires the global mobile ecosystem to mandate standard TLS encryption across all OEM keyboard components.

talks.title: Stranger in a Changed Land
talks.teaser: Reflects on a 35-year NSA career in defensive vulnerability analysis and the evolution of cybersecurity standards like the Critical Security Controls.
talks.summary:
A 35-Year NSA Career in Defense

Reflections from an executive manager at the National Security Agency chronicle thirty-five years of federal service dedicated to defensive vulnerability analysis and information assurance.

The Evolution of Cybersecurity Focus

Cyber defense paradigms evolved from early mathematical cryptography and government communications security to enterprise software systems and the global open internet.

Bridging Product Testing to Operational Guidance

Translating technical insights gained from red team testing and vulnerability research into actionable best practices led to the public release of NSA Security Guides.

Founding the Critical Security Controls

Collaborative efforts across public and private sectors established the CIS Critical Security Controls, providing automated, prioritized defensive baselines for global organizations.

talks.title: Inside the FBI’s Secret Encrypted Phone Company ‘Anom’
talks.teaser: Investigates the FBI's undercover operation running the encrypted phone app Anom, detailing the platform backdoor and law enforcement network compromise.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Anom in Organized Crime

In 2018, an encrypted communications application called Anom became widely adopted among global criminal syndicates, operating under the assumption of absolute privacy.

Undercover FBI Infrastructure and Backdoors

Unknown to users, the entire Anom telecommunications platform was secretly developed, managed, and monitored by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

Technical Architecture of the Network Tap

Investigative reporting reveals how the custom cryptographic backdoor functioned, secretly copying and relaying millions of encrypted messages to law enforcement monitoring centers.

Implications of Government Managed Backdoors

The operation marks a new era in global surveillance where authorities establish entire compromised telecom products, raising crucial questions about privacy and systemic supply chain trust.

talks.title: Joe & Bruno Hack Time: Regenerate Passwords from RoboForm's Password Generator
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers vintage RoboForm password generator routines to exploit weak PRNG randomness and recover millions in locked Bitcoin wallets.
talks.summary:
Recovering Locked Cryptocurrency Wallets

Security researchers Joe Grand and Bruno Krauss investigated recovering over three million dollars in Bitcoin trapped in an encrypted software wallet protected by a forgotten password.

Reverse Engineering RoboForm PRNG

Reverse engineering legacy versions of the RoboForm password manager using Ghidra, Cheat Engine, and x64dbg uncovered predictable pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) seeding.

Reconstructing Past Password States

Because the password generator tied its PRNG seed to the exact system clock timestamp, researchers built a custom tool to generate all possible password permutations within a target time window.

Responsible Disclosure and Password Security

While the flaw was fixed in subsequent RoboForm releases, the research highlights the enduring risks of weak entropy in cryptographic password generation.

talks.title: Hacking Millions of Modems and Investigating Who Hacked My Modem
talks.teaser: Chronicles an investigation into a compromised home modem that led to discovering centralized ISP vulnerabilities exposing millions of broadband devices.
talks.summary:
Discovering a Compromised Personal Modem

After observing suspicious replayed network traffic, security researcher Sam Curry investigated his personal ISP-provided home cable modem to understand how it was breached.

Uncovering Centralized ISP Vulnerabilities

Three years of web and hardware research revealed critical architecture flaws in centralized broadband management platforms used by major Internet Service Providers.

Arbitrary Remote Command Execution at Scale

Exploiting discovered vulnerabilities allowed unauthorized access to passively monitor customer traffic, rewrite configuration parameters, and execute arbitrary commands across millions of ISP modems.

Centralization Risks in Broadband Infrastructure

The findings emphasize the dangerous systemic risks created when millions of consumer edge devices are managed through centralized, unsegmented telecommunications backends.
